text:
sandeep: Reopened the PR with the requested changes applied. Addressed the allocator edge-case and added a unit test + bumped the e2e timeout. PTAL when you have a sec — planning to merge today if there are no objections.

maya: Quick q — the PR adds a small sleep in the harness, does that affect shard fallback timing in prod?

sandeep: Nope, the sleep is only in the test harness. Runtime path is unchanged; fallback uses non-blocking backoff. Example in the test stub: `// test-only sleep to expose race`
```
// test harness only
sleep(20)
assert(allocator.rotate())
```

olivia: Can you share perf numbers? a small regression at p95 would block the rollout.

sandeep: Ran a short 10k request perf run on staging: baseline median ~12.1ms -> new ~12.5ms, p95 stayed ~47ms. Runs: 12.0, 12.3, 12.4, p95 47.1. Looks like noise. Also gated behind `enable_new_alloc=true` flag for canary.

ci-bot: CI: build passed (linux/mac/unit). e2e had one unrelated py3 flaky test. Details: <ci/build/1739032100>

devon: @sandeep can you squash the test-fix commit into the feature commit? prefer 1 commit for cherry-pick.

sandeep: Yep — will squash and push, then re-request review.

maya: :eyes: I'll take a quick look after the squash.

olivia: :thumbsup: LGTM assuming you squash and add a short changelog note. No perf blocker from my side.

sandeep: Squashed and force-pushed, CI re-ran. PTAL @maya @olivia — thanks!

ci-bot: CI: all checks green on rerun.

maya: :heavy_check_mark: Looks good to me.

olivia: :thumbsup: approve

sandeep: Merging in 10m if no objections.
